family.name: Product Manager
family.summary: Retention dropped after a release and the CEO wants a feature for a big customer: find the real cause in the data, decide what the team builds next, and catch the holes in a junior PM’s spec.

stages.title: Warm-up
stages.summary: A 45-second spontaneous answer. Not scored; gives a voice sample to compare with later recordings.

stages.title: Why is retention down?
stages.summary: Find the cause of a retention drop hidden in the averages: Android new users after a sign-up change, with OTP tickets spiking. Think aloud.

stages.title: What gets built next
stages.summary: Choose how to spend six engineer-weeks with the CEO pushing for a customer feature. Think aloud.

stages.title: Three weeks in
stages.summary: Their plan meets reality. Tests adapting and stakeholder management.

stages.title: Review a junior PM's spec
stages.summary: A one-page spec with a vanity success metric, no segment, scope creep and no rollout plan. Think aloud.

stages.title: Update to the CEO (AI allowed)
stages.summary: Write the cycle plan update to the CEO with AI. Catches vague trade-offs and invented numbers.

stages.title: A product call you got wrong
stages.summary: A real product decision that did not work. Checks specificity and ownership.

brief.text: You're the Product Manager at **LearnNest**, an exam-prep app for school students, with 2,30,000 monthly active students. 72% of them use Android. Your quarterly goal is **week-4 retention**: the share of new students who have finished a lesson in their fourth week.
Release 3.2 shipped 5 weeks ago with a new sign-up flow (phone number and OTP first, then permissions). Since then, the headline number has fallen.
Support tickets tagged "OTP not received" went from 32 a week to 201 a week after the release.

rows: Teacher dashboards for a 120-school education chain (1,300 users)
Fix videos buffering on slow connections
Investigate and fix the new sign-up flow on Android

brief.text: You have **6 engineer-weeks** in the next cycle. The CEO has promised the big customer something "within 4 weeks".
The company and numbers are fictional, and every candidate gets a slightly different version. A calculator is fine.

prompt.text: Tell us about a feature you think should be removed from a product you use.
Keep it under 45 seconds. This one is not scored; it just gets you talking.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: **What do you think is causing the drop, and how would you confirm it this week?** Say what you would look at first.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

choices.label: Fix the Android onboarding first, then the support complaint
Build the CEO's feature for the big customer
Split the team: half on onboarding, half on the CEO’s feature
Spend two weeks on research before committing to anything

prompt.text: **How do you use the 6 engineer-weeks?** Pick one, then explain what you are saying no to and how you'll tell the CEO.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Fix the Android onboarding first, then the support complaint"

prompt.text: The fix shipped: OTP auto-read was broken on several Android versions. New-user week-1 activity is up, but week-4 retention won't be known for a month. Meanwhile the CEO forwards an email from a 120-school education chain: "If we don't see teacher dashboards soon we'll look elsewhere."
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Build the CEO's feature for the big customer"

prompt.text: The feature is half-built and slipping by a week. Android week-4 retention has fallen another 2 points, and your manager asks in the leadership meeting why the quarterly goal is going backwards.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Split the team: half on onboarding, half on the CEO’s feature"

prompt.text: Neither half is finished: the onboarding fix needs one more week, and the CEO’s feature is 40% done. Two engineers say context-switching is killing them.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

variants.label: If they chose "Spend two weeks on research before committing to anything"

prompt.text: Research confirms the OTP problem on Android, which the data already suggested. Two weeks have passed with nothing shipped, about 402 more OTP tickets have come in, and the CEO asks what the team has been doing.
**What do you do now?**

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

prompt.text: A junior PM wrote this spec for the sign-up fix. **Name the three most important problems, worst first, and why each matters.** Then rewrite the success metric.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

items: **Problem:** Users find sign-up confusing. Quotes from 3 students: "too many steps", "why do you need my location?", "OTP took forever".
**Goal:** Increase app downloads by 20% this quarter.
**Scope:** Redesign all sign-up screens with the new brand colours, add Google and Facebook login, add a referral code field, and fix OTP auto-read.
**Rollout:** Ship to 100% of users on both platforms next sprint.

prompt.text: Use any AI tool you like for this one. We are assessing how you use it, not whether you do.
Write your update to the CEO (under 200 words): the plan for the next cycle, what is not happening and why, and what you are offering the big customer.

items: Paste your full AI conversation, or write "none".
In 2–3 lines, say what you kept, changed or rejected from the AI and why.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.

stages.title: A product call you got wrong

prompt.text: **Tell us about a product decision you made that turned out wrong.** What did you see, what did you do, and what would you do differently?
Specifics such as numbers and timelines matter more than polish.

reviewerGuide.text: The answer key and rubric are hidden in the demo. Start free to see them for every role.
